Subject: PagerLess renewal proposal and upcoming price adjustment

Lauren —

- Term: 12 months starting 2027-07-01
- Seats: 150 active seats (with 10% overage buffer)
- Price: list +6% on list vs last year; we can hold at +3% if you sign by 2027-06-15
- SLA: 99.9% availability for control plane; statuspage uptime covered separately
- Data retention: 365 days by default; extended retention available as add-on

Attachments: PagerLess_Renewal_Proposal_2027-05-22.pdf

Tom —

Thanks for the proposal. A few immediate asks before we schedule an executive review:

1) Pricing breakout: please provide per-seat and per-month breakout and clarify what triggers overage billing (concurrent vs. total seats).
2) SLA: 99.9% control-plane availability is lower than our target for core paging. We need to see options for 99.95% or a credits schedule that scales (example: 99.9% -> 2% credits, 99.5% -> 5% credits).
3) Security evidence: please share the latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted ok) and a current subprocessor list. We require SOC2 and full subprocessor disclosure for Private deployments.
4) Data retention: call out retention of audit logs and incident transcripts. Our legal/compliance will want explicit deletion/archival terms.
5) PO/contract path: who is the contracting contact and do you accept Net 30 via PO?

Dev, Steph — looping you in for API/sync questions and pricing alignment.

If you can get the SOC2 and a per-line pricing table by EOD Wed (2027-05-26) we can accelerate the internal approval.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Sarah/Tom —

Quick technical clarifications before we commit to SLA/99.95% wording: 
1) API rate limits: please provide burst vs sustained rate limits (rpm and rps) for the control plane and for event ingestion (webhooks). We ingest ~3k events/day now, peaking ~250 events/min during incidents.
2) KV cache / incident context: does PagerLess persist KV for automated runbooks between incidents or is that ephemeral? We rely on your KV to persist short-term incident metadata; losing that would break our automations.
3) Webhooks and delivery semantics: do you guarantee at-least-once or exactly-once delivery? We have idempotency keys in our consumers but need delivery window SLA.
4) Statuspage integration: we push status updates to a private status page; confirm retention and access controls for status snapshot history (inc. ability to export).
5) SecOps needs: we will require a 30-day incident log export in JSON for audits and a documented data deletion procedure.

If you can put answers in bullet form and call out any exceptions (e.g., long-term KV persistence is a paid add-on), that will help legal/pricing. Happy to do a 30-min technical sync Wed 2027-05-26 10:00 PT if that works.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
